judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header's search toggle: a visually hidden (sr-only) checkbox with aria-label="Abrir busca", operated through <label for="acritica-search-toggle"> whose visible content at desktop width is the text "Buscar" plus an aria-hidden magnifier icon (the screenshot shows "Buscar" with the icon at the top right of the blue header). claimTrue: the snapshot shows exactly this, the aria-label overrides the label so the accessible name is "Abrir busca" (nameFrom aria-label), and "Buscar" does not occur in it; calling a checkbox a "field" is loose wording, not a false statement. elementFails: the component's visible label is "Buscar" and its accessible name "Abrir busca" does not contain that text ("busca" is a different word from "Buscar", and a speech user saying "click Buscar" targets a name that does not hold it), which is failure F96 of 2.5.3. captureDiffers: the live HTML fetched now has the same label, the same checkbox and the same aria-label, and no script changes them (the toggle works by CSS peer-checked); the screenshot is fully styled. The claim names this failure, so the label is true_positive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the h1 of the homepage's lead story, inside the story link, "Praia da Ponta Negra é interditada para banho em Manaus". claimTrue: the content it heads in the snapshot and screenshot is the dek "Interdição foi anunciada após o rio Negro atingir 15,94 metros; medida segue recomendação do Serviço Geológico do Brasil" and the byline, which are about the same topic; what follows are three separate story links (Maria do Carmo, a car overturning, tranças afro) in a related-stories list without headings, which do not make the heading name a different topic than its own content, so the sentence does not hold. elementFails: the heading describes the story it introduces, and the destination page carries the same headline, so it meets 2.4.6; the unheaded list after it (and the use of an h1 for a teaser on a homepage) is at most a structure question, not a non-descriptive heading. captureDiffers: the live page has the same lead story, headline and dek (only the relative time moved from 5 to 6 hours). The model had the dek in the link's text and judged wrongly, so the label is false_positive with cause model_error.
